title: Adobe camera app’s new feature will critique your photos using AI
slides: Can Adobe’s AI finally fix your worst photos?
It analyzes composition, lighting, and focus instantly.
But it won’t tell you the best crop—yet.
Editors now get instant feedback before sharing.
Upload a favorite image and compare its critique.
thread_text:
1. AI sees your mistakes.

Adobe's tool analyzes composition, lighting, and focus instantly—finding flaws you might miss.

2. The blind spot.

It can't tell you the best crop. Judgment on framing still needs a human eye.

3. Feedback before sharing.

Editors now get instant analysis before posting, cutting revision cycles short.

4. Test it yourself.

Upload a favorite image and compare its critique to your own. The gap reveals what you overlook.

5. Try the crop test.

Take one of your photos, ask the AI for feedback, then choose the crop yourself. Does it match your instinct?

instagram.caption:
That new Adobe camera app can spot your bad composition or lighting in seconds—before you even hit share.

It checks focus, exposure, and structure instantly. You get feedback while you still have time to adjust.

But it won’t choose the crop for you. That judgment stays with the human eye.

For editors and casual shooters, it means fewer revisions and faster posts.

Upload your own best photo: does the AI critique what you see, or does it reveal what you missed? ✍️
